issues.where: O god, of Pururāvan, protect (me) from harm
issues.problem: "pururāvṇaḥ" is treated as a name qualifying deva ("god of Pururāvan"); nothing in the unit says so. A genitive/ablative beside pāhi ... riṣaḥ (ablative) is more natural as a second ablative ("from ...") and its sense is open. summary: 31 units (33-63) reviewed; 19 errors, 21 minor; 7 issues without a machine patch (MANUAL); no regrouping suggested. Main problems: bracketed glosses in Hindi, unit 46 (garbled, yavyā), unit 48 (pururāvṇaḥ read as a name), unit 37 (narya vs nārya), additions (your sister, mountain, come). Proposed glossary: karma = rite (ritual act) in this Samhita; vipra = inspired one (not ṛṣi/sage); no brackets in Hindi even for supplied words.
